Finding and consequence: **A booked price can increase without consent.** Staff item edits replace the bill immediately; customers receive the changed total after the change. Unchanged garments also acquire today's catalogue rate.
Correction and acceptance: Preserve existing quoted rates. Show old/new counts, rates, discount, fees, total, reason and delta. Require approval for an increase; apply decreases with a notice. No collection of an unapproved increase.

Finding and consequence: **A pending refund can be presented as sent.** Tracking compares aggregate `refundedPaise` with paid money, but that aggregate includes PENDING refunds. It also assumes the original account for refunds that may be recorded as cash/bank transfer. Partial refunds are described using the original paid amount.
Correction and acceptance: Render each refund's method, amount and PENDING/PROCESSED/FAILED status from the refund records already returned. Show paid, completed refund, pending refund and remaining amount separately. Never label a pending request as completed.

Finding and consequence: **The receipt screen asserts success without validating the order state.** With no order, it says “Paid” and “Your payment is done”; with any order, it says fully paid. A direct receipt route, failed fetch or stale order can therefore give false reassurance. The normal payment path does wait for confirmation, which reduces exposure but does not make this screen safe independently.
Correction and acceptance: Loading, retry/error, outstanding-balance and confirmed-paid states must be explicit. Require a confirmed paid state before showing the success message, including on direct navigation and refresh.

Finding and consequence: **Receipt details are not a transaction receipt.** “When” uses `DateTime.now()` on render; the amount is cumulative order payment, not necessarily the just-completed balance payment. Reopening changes the apparent transaction time.
Correction and acceptance: Display the payment record's confirmed time, provider reference and transaction amount; label cumulative order payment separately. Reopening must preserve the same transaction details. Requires a customer-safe payment DTO if no existing customer endpoint provides it.

Finding and consequence: **Items and bill has no fetch-error recovery.** With no initial order, a failed request remains a spinner; with an initial order, stale content has no refresh-failed indication. Its header maps a fully refunded, zero-due order to “Unpaid.”
Correction and acceptance: Handle loading/error/retry/stale explicitly. Render PAID, PARTIALLY_PAID, UNPAID and REFUNDED accurately. A failed direct bill load must offer Retry and Back.

Finding and consequence: **The displayed payment method is guessed from order choice and delivery status.** A COD order paid online before delivery can later say “Paid in cash”; a split cash/online order cannot be represented accurately. Payment capture does not rewrite the original order method.
Correction and acceptance: Use actual captured payment records or a server-computed payment summary. Correctly distinguish online, cash and mixed payment after delivery.

Finding and consequence: **Units become misleading outside the catalogue.** The catalogue supports piece/pair/set/kg, but basket prices say “each,” summary quantities are added as item counts, and quantities are integer-only. An order of kilograms is presented like a garment count and 2.5 kg cannot be entered.
Correction and acceptance: Carry units through basket/bill/receipt/admin. For launch, either explicitly sell whole-kg increments or hide KG until measured-weight billing is implemented. Do not sum kilograms and garment pieces into one physical count.

Finding and consequence: **Call/email actions lack launch-failure recovery.** The shared support helper discards `launchUrl`'s boolean result and screens do not provide a useful fallback. A device without an email/phone handler can leave the customer with no next step.
Correction and acceptance: Catch failure, show the contact in selectable/copyable form and offer the other available channel. Denied/unavailable handlers must not silently fail or surface an unhandled exception.

Finding and consequence: **Order help does not carry order context into email.** The sheet tells customers to mention the order number, but the email link contains only the recipient. Customers must retype an ID already known to the app.
Correction and acceptance: Prefill a subject/body with order number and issue prompt; retain a manual contact fallback. Do not include more personal data than needed.

Finding and consequence: **Edit items previews only subtotal before discount.** Staff cannot review the old versus proposed final payable total, fee/discount changes or the additional/refundable amount before Save. This amplifies C01.
Correction and acceptance: Reuse a server quote for the proposed edit; show before/after/delta and approval state. Saving a higher amount must request consent rather than silently replace the accepted bill.

Finding and consequence: **Price-preservation copy contradicts item editing.** Catalogue and settings say existing orders retain prices, while `updateItems` reprices all submitted lines at current rates. Staff may change the rate card believing old orders are protected.
Correction and acceptance: Freeze booked line rates; until fixed, make the edit consequence explicit. Acceptance: changing today's catalogue must not alter an unchanged line on an existing order.

Finding and consequence: **Cash collection is preconfirmed for COD orders.** The delivered dialog starts with the cash-collected box checked, so a routine confirmation can record money staff did not actually receive. It also retains component state between dialog openings.
Correction and acceptance: Start each delivery confirmation unanswered. Require an explicit Paid in cash / Not collected choice when money is due, show the amount, and preserve a deliberate unpaid-delivery path.

Finding and consequence: **“Today” KPI links do not show the counted records.** Orders placed today opens all orders; pickup/delivery cards select workflow tabs without today's date. Pickup-date filtering alone cannot reproduce the delivery-date KPI. Partners online opens all partners.
Correction and acceptance: Each KPI must open a list using the identical date/status definition, including completed pickups/deliveries if the count includes them. Implement the missing created/delivery-date filters.

Finding and consequence: **The no-partner queue can disappear on error.** Its query is independent of the main dashboard; only successful nonempty data renders a panel. A healthy KPI response plus a failed attention query can look like no work needs attention.
Correction and acceptance: Always show an explicit loading/current/failed/stale state for the exception queue and a Retry action. A fetch error must never look like zero exceptions.

Finding and consequence: **Alerts say “All caught up” before successful loading and on fetch failure.** Missing data defaults unread to zero; the sheet has no loading, error or retry branch.
Correction and acceptance: Show loading/error separately from a confirmed empty inbox; retain stale alerts visibly when refresh fails.

Finding and consequence: **Only the latest 30 staff alerts are reachable.** There is no next page/load-more control even though the unread count can exceed that window. Mark all read can acknowledge alerts that the operator could not inspect in this UI.
Correction and acceptance: Add pagination/load more and distinguish “mark visible read” from “mark all read,” with clear scope. Verify an older unread refund alert is reachable.

Finding and consequence: **Item editing and partner assignment have no query-error branch.** Their dialogs show a skeleton whenever data is absent, including a rejected request. Staff have to close and reopen without knowing why it failed.
Correction and acceptance: Add local error/retry states and preserve entered quantities/selection. Submission must require successfully loaded source data.

Finding and consequence: **Realtime recovery is not visible or explicitly refreshed.** The bridge handles `order.updated` only. There is no reconnect invalidation or connection-status indicator; order lists/details have no periodic refetch of their own. Focus refetch may eventually repair stale data, but a continuously open disconnected tab has no such guarantee.
Correction and acceptance: On reconnect, invalidate visible operational queries; expose connection/last-refresh status and manual Refresh. Test a missed update during disconnect.

Finding and consequence: **Order editing labels every rate “each” and totals all units as pieces.** The new-order item chooser does respect units, so two admin flows describe the same service differently.
Correction and acceptance: Share unit formatting and unit-aware summaries with C07; verify a piece, pair, set and KG item in both admin flows.

Finding and consequence: **Partner onboarding instructs staff to use an app that is not built.** Empty states say partners sign in/go online in the partner app; assignment copy says it is looking automatically. The runbook says staff currently do every transition.
Correction and acceptance: Describe the current manual workflow and show an explicit dispatch mode. Keep the selected Flutter partner-app plan, but do not imply it works before field validation.

Finding and consequence: **Unsaved work can be dismissed without a warning.** Settings has a dirty-state message and Discard, but no navigation guard; item/promotion/banner dialogs close on ordinary dismissal without a dirty-state check.
Correction and acceptance: Warn on leaving a dirty form or provide a recoverable local draft. Do not add confirmations when nothing changed. Preserve work after a failed save.

Finding and consequence: **Switching the phone-order customer silently carries the previous draft.** `selectCustomer` clears only address selection; items, notes, promo and schedule remain. A different customer's instructions can be submitted with a newly selected customer.
Correction and acceptance: On a nonempty draft, offer “Start a new order” or explicitly retain a clearly labeled draft; clear customer-specific notes/promo/address by default. Show customer and contact in the final review.

Finding and consequence: **Every confirmation uses “Keep it” as its cancel action.** That wording is ambiguous for Mark delivered, refunds and other actions that are not retaining an object.
Correction and acceptance: Allow context-specific cancel labels, such as “Go back” or “Don't mark delivered”; keep “Keep order” where appropriate.

Finding and consequence: **The dashboard chart has no equivalent accessible per-day data.** Counts are revealed on mouse hover; the graphic's accessible label gives only a generic description. Exact dates/values are not available in a keyboard-operable detail view.
Correction and acceptance: Add an accessible date/count/value table or keyboard-operable details. Keep the simple chart; a charting framework is unnecessary.

Finding and consequence: **Audit details are abbreviated raw JSON without an accessible detail view.** The table truncates at 140 characters and relies on a title tooltip for the full payload; no search/actor/entity/date filters exist. This makes resolving a changed bill unnecessarily difficult.
Correction and acceptance: Add a readable expandable record with before/after fields and basic filters. Keep pagination. A keyboard or touch user must be able to inspect the full relevant event.

Finding and consequence: **Phone-order retries can create duplicates.** The customer endpoint supports an idempotency key, but the admin endpoint does not accept/pass one and the new-order client does not send one. A server commit followed by a lost response leaves staff with an unsafe retry.
Correction and acceptance: Use one persistent key per admin draft/attempt and return the original result on retry. Verify a committed request with a deliberately lost response produces exactly one order.

Finding and consequence: **Concurrent item edits have no revision-conflict protection.** The replacement checks only the current status. Two staff editing an order in the same status can overwrite each other's quantities without a conflict; the UI has no revision warning.
Correction and acceptance: Add an expected revision/updated-at check or equivalent atomic conflict guard. On conflict, show fresh versus draft items and let staff reconcile; never blindly replay the replacement.
